previous_assumption: getRental(userId, rentalCompanyOrganizationId, rentalId) always required rental.manage regardless of caller organization type
correction: rental.manage is rental_company-only per PERMISSION_ORGANIZATION_TYPES, so this made it literally impossible for ANY Renter to ever call getRental successfully, no matter their role/permissions — not a custom-role edge case, every Renter viewing a Transport or Logsheet detail page for their own rental hit this. Fixed to branch by the caller's own organization type, mirroring listRentals' existing branch: rental_company needs rental.manage, renter needs rental.respond and gets machine/rental-company names resolved server-side. Caught while auditing custom-role permission gaps, not by an explicit renter bug report — worth checking any other single-resource 'getX' method for the same 'always requires the rental_company-side permission' mistake its sibling listX method already avoided.

previous_assumption: A new two-sided verification mechanism (Rental Company records actual dates, Renter confirms) could reuse Logsheet's customerConfirmed pattern -- a plain boolean set only by the Rental Company
correction: customerConfirmed has no counterparty write path at all (logsheet.respond is read-only) and no dispute path -- it is self-attested, not verified. The client explicitly asked for a real two-sided mechanism this time. Modeled the new actualDatesVerificationStatus after QuotationOffer's pending/accepted/rejected shape instead: rental.manage auto-captures actualStartDate/actualEndDate on the active/off_rent transition (defaults to today, overridable), then rental.respond gets explicit verifyActualDates/disputeActualDates(reason) actions gated on status===pending.
